models.name: todo_app_users
models.description:
Registered user accounts with email/password authentication credentials and profile information. This table serves as the primary actor entity for authenticated users who manage their personal todo lists. Users can create, edit, complete, and delete todos while maintaining complete privacy and data isolation from other users. Each user has a profile with display name and authentication credentials for secure login and account management.

The table supports user registration, login, password changes, and account deletion workflows. It maintains temporal tracking for creation, updates, and soft deletion capabilities. All user data is completely isolated, ensuring privacy guarantees as specified in the requirements.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address used for authentication and account identification. Must be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for user authentication. Stored using industry-standard hashing algorithms.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's display name shown throughout the application for personalization and identification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was soft deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: todo_app_user_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for user authentication with access and refresh token support. Each session tracks the user's login context including IP address, browser information, and connection metadata for security auditing purposes.

Sessions are created during user login and managed through authentication flows. They contain both access and refresh tokens to support secure authentication with token rotation. The expiration tracking ensures sessions are automatically invalidated after their designated lifetime for security.

This table maintains a complete audit trail of user login activity, supporting security monitoring and compliance requirements. Sessions are automatically cleaned up based on expiration policies to maintain database performance and security.

{@link todo_app_users.id}

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: Authenticated user's session reference. {@link todo_app_users.id}

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for authenticated API requests. Contains user identity and permissions encoded as a secure token.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without requiring re-authentication. Used for session longevity.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client connection where the session was created. Used for security auditing and geographic tracking.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page where the session was initiated. Provides context for the login event.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer header value indicating the source page that directed to the login. Useful for traffic source analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created during user login. Used for session lifetime calculation and audit trail.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid. Ensures automatic session cleanup for security.

models.name: todo_app_user_password_resets
models.description: Stores password reset tokens with expiration timestamps for secure password recovery workflow. Each reset request generates a unique token that can be used once to reset a user's password within a limited time window for security purposes. Users can have multiple reset requests over time, but only active (unexpired, unused) tokens are valid for password reset operations.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: User who requested the password reset. {@link todo_app_users.id}

plainFields.name: reset_token
plainFields.description: Unique cryptographic token for password reset verification. Must be cryptographically secure and globally unique.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token expires and becomes invalid for security purposes.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token was successfully used to reset password. Null indicates unused token.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset record was soft deleted for audit purposes.

models.name: todo_app_system_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings and parameters for application operation.

Stores key-value pairs that control various aspects of the application behavior, including feature flags, system-wide settings, performance parameters, and operational configurations. Each configuration entry has a unique key and supports type-safe values through separate data type tables.

Maintains audit trail capabilities through reference to {@link todo_app_system_metadata.id} for logging configuration changes and system administration purposes. System administrators can modify these settings to control application behavior without requiring code changes.

This table serves as the primary configuration registry, with actual values stored in type-specific subsidiary tables to ensure data integrity and type safety.

foreignFields.name: system_metadata_id
foreignFields.description: Associated system metadata entry for audit trail and change tracking. Referenced system metadata's {@link todo_app_system_metadata.id}.

plainFields.name: config_key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key identifier used to reference this setting throughout the application.

plainFields.name: value_type
plainFields.description: Data type of the configuration value: 'string', 'boolean', 'number', 'json'. Defines which subsidiary table contains the actual value.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration entry was last modified.

models.name: todo_app_audit_logs
models.description:
Comprehensive audit trail for security events and system operations.

Records system-wide audit events including user authentication attempts, data modifications, system configuration changes, and security incidents. Each entry includes timestamp, event type, user context (when applicable), source IP address, and detailed event description. Supports compliance requirements and forensic investigation capabilities.

Tracks both automated system events and user-initiated operations. Events are categorized by severity and type to enable targeted monitoring and alerting. Audit entries are append-only and cannot be modified or deleted to maintain audit trail integrity.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User who performed the audited action, if applicable. Null for system-initiated or anonymous events. {@link todo_app_users.id}

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Category of the audit event (e.g., authentication, data_modification, system_configuration, security_incident).

plainFields.name: event_subtype
plainFields.description: Specific subcategory of the event for detailed classification (e.g., login_success, login_failure, create_todo, update_todo).

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of the event (info, warning, error, critical) for filtering and alerting purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the audit event including specific actions performed and relevant context.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: Source IP address from which the event originated.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: HTTP user agent string from the client that initiated the event.

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: Identifier of the specific resource affected by the event (e.g., todo ID for todo modifications).

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: Type of resource affected by the event (e.g., todo, user, system_configuration).

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Additional JSON-formatted metadata providing context-specific details about the event.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit event was recorded by the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit entry was last updated (typically same as created_at for audit trails).

models.name: todo_app_system_metadata
models.description:
Tracks metadata for system operations, maintenance activities, and version control. This table serves as the central repository for system operational metadata, recording information about maintenance windows, system updates, configuration changes, and operational events. Each entry captures the type of operation, associated version information, status tracking, and audit trail data.

Key relationships include references to system configuration tables for operational context and maintenance windows for scheduled operations. The metadata supports audit trails, compliance requirements, and operational monitoring across the application infrastructure.

This table is essential for maintaining system reliability, tracking operational changes, and providing comprehensive audit capabilities for system administrators.

plainFields.name: operation_type
plainFields.description: Type of system operation being tracked (e.g., maintenance, update, configuration_change, backup, migration).

plainFields.name: operation_version
plainFields.description: Version identifier for the operation, typically following semantic versioning or internal versioning schemes.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the operation (e.g., pending, in_progress, completed, failed, rolled_back).

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the operation, including purpose, scope, and any relevant notes.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the operation was initiated or scheduled to begin.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the operation was completed or finalized.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the metadata record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the metadata record was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_error_logs

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: User session where the error occurred. {@link todo_app_users.id}

foreignFields.name: user_session_id
foreignFields.description: Specific session instance where the error occurred. {@link todo_app_user_sessions.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the error occurred and was logged.

plainFields.name: error_type

plainFields.name: error_message

plainFields.name: stack_trace

plainFields.name: request_path

plainFields.name: request_parameters

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string from the client that triggered the error.

plainFields.name: ip_address

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the error was marked as resolved or handled.

models.name: todo_app_feature_flags
models.description:
Manages feature flags for controlled feature deployments and A/B testing capabilities.

Feature flags enable gradual rollout of new features, selective user targeting, and controlled experimentation without requiring code deployments. Each flag can be independently configured with targeting rules, rollout percentages, and activation status to precisely control feature availability.

This table supports A/B testing by tracking feature flag assignments and ensuring consistent user experiences across sessions. Flags can be configured for global enablement, user segmentation, percentage-based rollout, or targeted activation based on specific criteria.

**Important**: Feature flags are managed independently of application code, allowing operations teams to control feature availability in real-time without developer intervention.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the feature flag used in application code.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining the feature flag's purpose and usage.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Indicates whether the feature flag is currently active and should be evaluated.

plainFields.name: rollout_percentage
plainFields.description: Percentage of users (0-100) for whom the feature should be enabled during gradual rollout.

plainFields.name: target_scope
plainFields.description: Scope definition specifying targeting criteria (global, user-based, percentage-based, etc.).

plainFields.name: targeting_rules
plainFields.description: JSON configuration detailing specific targeting criteria and activation conditions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the feature flag was initially created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the feature flag configuration was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the feature flag was soft-deleted (for cleanup and audit purposes).

models.name: todo_app_api_rate_limits
models.description:
API rate limiting configuration and enforcement tracking.

This table manages rate limiting policies for different API endpoints, user types, and access scopes. It tracks both configuration settings and real-time usage to enforce API rate limits effectively. Each entry defines a specific rate limiting policy with its enforcement parameters and tracks current usage within the defined time windows.

Rate limiting rules cascade from most specific to general: per-user limits override global limits, endpoint-specific limits override general API limits. The system uses this table to determine when to throttle requests and track enforcement events for auditing purposes.

plainFields.name: rate_limit_name
plainFields.description: Descriptive name for this rate limiting rule for administrative reference.

plainFields.name: rate_limit_type
plainFields.description: Type of rate limit: global, user_level, endpoint_specific, or ip_based.

plainFields.name: requests_limit
plainFields.description: Maximum number of requests allowed within the specified time window.

plainFields.name: time_window_seconds
plainFields.description: Time window in seconds during which the requests limit applies.

plainFields.name: scope_identifier
plainFields.description: Optional identifier for the scope (endpoint path, user_id, IP address, or '*').

plainFields.name: current_usage_count
plainFields.description: Current number of requests counted within the current time window.

plainFields.name: window_start_time
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the current measurement window started.

plainFields.name: is_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this rate limiting rule is currently active and enforced.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of this rate limiting rule's purpose and usage.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rate limiting rule was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this rate limiting rule was last modified.

models.name: todo_app_system_health_checks
models.description:
System health monitoring and status tracking for availability monitoring. Stores health check results from various system components including database connectivity, API endpoints, external service dependencies, and internal system metrics. Each health check record represents a point-in-time assessment of system health with detailed status information and diagnostic data.

Health checks are performed at regular intervals to monitor system availability and performance. The table tracks check types, status values, response times, error details, and metadata for comprehensive monitoring and alerting. This data supports system reliability analysis, performance monitoring, and proactive issue detection.

Related entities include {@link todo_app_system_configurations} for health check configuration settings and {@link todo_app_error_logs} for correlating health check failures with system errors.

plainFields.name: check_type
plainFields.description: Type of health check being performed (e.g., 'database', 'api', 'external_service', 'internal_system').

plainFields.name: check_name
plainFields.description: Specific name identifier for the health check (e.g., 'postgres_connection', 'api_health_endpoint', 'payment_gateway').

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Health check result status (e.g., 'healthy', 'degraded', 'unhealthy', 'timeout', 'error').

plainFields.name: response_time
plainFields.description: Response time in milliseconds for the health check operation. Null if check failed or timed out.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Detailed error message if the health check failed. Null for successful checks.

plainFields.name: check_timestamp
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the health check was performed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this health check record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this health check record was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_background_jobs
models.description:
Background job scheduling and execution tracker for system operations.

This table manages all background job processing including scheduling, execution status tracking, retry logic, and job lifecycle monitoring. It supports both system-generated and user-initiated background tasks.

Each job tracks scheduling parameters, execution timing, status transitions, and completion results. The system uses this table for job prioritization, failure recovery, and performance monitoring.

Relationships:
- References {@link todo_app_users.id} for job ownership and auditing
- No other foreign key relationships required for this systematic component

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner user who submitted or initiated this background job. {@link todo_app_users.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Descriptive name of the background job for identification and monitoring.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the job's purpose and operations.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current execution status of the job: 'pending', 'running', 'completed', 'failed', 'canceled'.

plainFields.name: parameters
plainFields.description: JSON-encoded parameters and configuration for the job execution.

plainFields.name: scheduled_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job is scheduled to start execution.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job execution actually began.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job execution completed or failed.

plainFields.name: retry_count
plainFields.description: Number of retry attempts made for this job.

plainFields.name: max_retries
plainFields.description: Maximum number of retry attempts allowed before permanent failure.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Error message captured when job execution fails.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Detailed reason for job failure, including stack traces if available.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the job was soft-deleted for cleanup.

models.name: todo_app_data_migrations
models.description:
Tracks data migration operations and schema changes for version control and audit purposes.

This table provides comprehensive tracking of all database migration operations executed on the system. It captures execution details, status changes, and error information to ensure reliable schema evolution management. Each migration is uniquely identified by name and version combination for precise version control.

Maintains audit trail for compliance and debugging purposes, recording execution timestamps, duration, and rollback capabilities. Supports reliable deployment workflows by tracking migration states including pending, running, completed, and failed statuses.

plainFields.name: migration_name
plainFields.description: Unique name identifier for the migration operation.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version identifier for ordering and dependency management.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current execution status of the migration: pending, running, completed, or failed.

plainFields.name: executed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the migration was executed, null if not yet executed.

plainFields.name: execution_duration
plainFields.description: Duration of migration execution in milliseconds, null if not executed.

plainFields.name: rollback_available
plainFields.description: Whether this migration can be rolled back if needed.

plainFields.name: error_details
plainFields.description: Detailed error information if migration failed, null if successful.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the migration purpose and changes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the migration tracking record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the migration tracking record was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_system_notifications
models.description:
System notification management and delivery tracking for application-wide notifications.

This table handles the complete lifecycle of system notifications including creation, delivery attempts, status tracking, and audit trails. Notifications can target specific users or be system-wide broadcasts. The system supports retry mechanisms for failed deliveries and maintains comprehensive tracking of notification states.

Notifications are categorized by type (system alerts, user notifications, maintenance announcements) and priority levels to ensure appropriate delivery handling. Each notification records delivery attempts, failures, and final status for audit purposes.

This infrastructure table supports application operations by providing reliable notification delivery while maintaining system stability and performance.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: Target user for personalized notifications. Nullable for system-wide broadcasts. {@link todo_app_users.id}

plainFields.name: notification_type
plainFields.description: Category of notification (system_alert, user_notification, maintenance, security, performance).

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Delivery priority level (low, normal, high, critical).

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: Notification subject line or title.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Full notification message content.

plainFields.name: delivery_status
plainFields.description: Current delivery status (pending, sent, delivered, failed, expired).

plainFields.name: delivery_method
plainFields.description: Delivery channel (email, in_app, push, sms, webhook).

plainFields.name: retry_count
plainFields.description: Number of delivery attempts made.

plainFields.name: max_retries
plainFields.description: Maximum allowed delivery attempts before marking as failed.

plainFields.name: last_attempt_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent delivery attempt.

plainFields.name: next_retry_at
plainFields.description: Scheduled time for next delivery attempt if retries remain.

plainFields.name: sent_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was successfully sent.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was confirmed delivered.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification expires and should not be delivered.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for delivery failure if applicable.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: Additional delivery metadata in JSON format.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_cache_managements
models.description:
Cache management system table responsible for cache configuration, invalidation tracking, and performance monitoring.

This table stores system-wide cache configurations including cache key patterns, invalidation rules, TTL settings, and performance metrics. It tracks cache hit/miss ratios, memory usage, and operational statistics to support caching optimization and monitoring across the application.

The cache management system provides centralized control over caching strategies, allowing configuration of distinct caching approaches for different data domains or API endpoints. As a subsidiary table, it supports the primary application functionality by optimizing performance without direct user interaction.

Performance metrics enable proactive optimization and debugging of caching behavior based on production usage patterns observed across the todo application ecosystem.

plainFields.name: cache_key_pattern
plainFields.description: Pattern template for cache keys used by this cache configuration. Examples: 'user_profile:{userId}', 'todo_list:{userId}:{status}', 'api_response:{endpoint}:{params}'. Must be unique across all configurations.

plainFields.name: cache_strategy
plainFields.description: Caching strategy applied (e.g., 'time_based', 'event_based', 'manual', 'hybrid'). Determines invalidation behavior and cache lifecycle management.

plainFields.name: time_to_live_seconds
plainFields.description: Time-to-live setting in seconds for automatic cache expiration. Null indicates manual invalidation strategy without automatic expiration.

plainFields.name: max_cache_size
plainFields.description: Maximum cache size in megabytes for this configuration. Null indicates no size limit for dynamic memory allocation.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this cache configuration is currently active and being applied across the application.

plainFields.name: last_invalidation_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent cache invalidation event for this configuration. Used for debugging and performance analysis.

plainFields.name: hit_count
plainFields.description: Total number of cache hits recorded for this configuration. Incremented on successful cache retrievals.

plainFields.name: miss_count
plainFields.description: Total number of cache misses recorded for this configuration. Incremented on cache misses requiring backend retrieval.

plainFields.name: average_response_time_ms
plainFields.description: Average response time in milliseconds for cache operations under this configuration. Calculated periodically from operational metrics.

plainFields.name: memory_usage_mb
plainFields.description: Current memory usage in megabytes for this cache configuration. Monitored for resource allocation and performance tuning.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cache configuration was initially created and activated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cache configuration was last modified, including performance metric updates or settings changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cache configuration was soft-deleted. Null indicates active configuration.

models.name: todo_app_maintenance_windows
models.description:
Tracks scheduled maintenance windows and system downtime events for the Todo application.

This table manages planned maintenance schedules and tracks actual downtime events. Each record represents a maintenance window with defined start and end times, status tracking, and impact assessment. Maintenance windows can be scheduled in advance or created for emergency downtime situations.

The table supports various maintenance window states including scheduled, active, completed, and canceled. It also tracks the impact level of maintenance events to help communicate system availability to users.

Maintenance windows are essential for system reliability and user communication, providing clear visibility into planned downtime and tracking actual system availability metrics.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Descriptive title of the maintenance window for identification and communication purposes.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the maintenance work being performed and its impact on users.

plainFields.name: scheduled_start_at
plainFields.description: Planned start time of the maintenance window when system changes will begin.

plainFields.name: scheduled_end_at
plainFields.description: Planned end time of the maintenance window when normal operations should resume.

plainFields.name: actual_start_at
plainFields.description: Actual start time when maintenance activities began, recorded for tracking purposes.

plainFields.name: actual_end_at
plainFields.description: Actual end time when maintenance activities completed and system resumed normal operations.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the maintenance window: scheduled, active, completed, or canceled.

plainFields.name: impact_level
plainFields.description: Impact level indicating the severity of system disruption: low, medium, high, or critical.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the maintenance window was initially scheduled and created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the maintenance window record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the maintenance window was soft-deleted, if applicable.

models.name: todo_app_system_configuration_strings
models.description:
Stores string-type configuration values with proper type safety and validation.

This table represents individual string configuration values within the system configuration management infrastructure. Each record stores a specific string value with validation metadata, ensuring type safety and data integrity for system configuration parameters.

Configuration values support various system operations including feature flags, application settings, and runtime parameters. The table maintains proper relationships with parent configuration entities while avoiding field duplication.

{@link todo_app_system_configurations.id} provides the parent configuration context for these string values.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_system_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Parent system configuration entity that owns this string value. {@link todo_app_system_configurations.id}

plainFields.name: configuration_value
plainFields.description: Actual string configuration value with proper validation and formatting.

plainFields.name: validation_pattern
plainFields.description: Regular expression pattern for validating the configuration value format.

plainFields.name: max_length
plainFields.description: Maximum allowed length for the configuration value.

plainFields.name: min_length
plainFields.description: Minimum required length for the configuration value.

models.name: todo_app_system_configuration_booleans
models.description:
Stores boolean-type configuration values with proper type safety and validation.

This table is part of the system configuration infrastructure and provides type-safe storage for boolean configuration parameters. Each record represents a specific boolean configuration value that can be used throughout the application. The table ensures proper validation and maintains referential integrity with the parent configuration registry.

Boolean configurations are typically used for feature flags, system toggles, and operational switches that control application behavior. The table supports the systematic component's configuration management system by providing specialized storage for boolean values with appropriate constraints.

Access temporal information and configuration metadata through the parent table {@link todo_app_system_configurations.id}

foreignFields.name: todo_app_system_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent system configuration entry. {@link todo_app_system_configurations.id}

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: The actual boolean configuration value. This field stores the true/false state that controls system behavior or feature flags.

models.name: todo_app_system_configuration_numbers
models.description:
Stores numeric configuration values with proper type safety and validation.

This table provides a dedicated storage mechanism for numeric system configuration values, ensuring type safety and validation constraints. Each record represents a specific numeric configuration setting that can be referenced by the main system configuration table.

Numeric configurations are used for system parameters that require mathematical operations, ranges, or specific numeric constraints. Examples include timeout values, threshold limits, capacity settings, and performance tuning parameters.

The table maintains referential integrity with the main system configurations table while providing specialized storage for numeric values with appropriate validation rules.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_system_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent system configuration entry. {@link todo_app_system_configurations.id}

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: The actual numeric configuration value. This field stores the numeric setting that can be used for system parameters requiring mathematical operations or specific numeric constraints.

models.name: todo_app_system_configuration_jsons
models.description:
Stores JSON configuration values with proper type safety and validation. This table holds complex configuration data in JSON format that requires structured validation and type safety enforcement. Each configuration value is associated with a system configuration entry for proper grouping and management.

JSON configuration values stored here can represent complex data structures like feature flag configurations, API endpoint settings, or system parameter groupings. The table includes validation metadata to ensure JSON schema compliance and proper type handling throughout the application.

This table works in conjunction with {@link todo_app_system_configurations} to provide a comprehensive configuration management system that supports both simple and complex configuration needs.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_system_configuration_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent system configuration entry. {@link todo_app_system_configurations.id}

plainFields.name: configuration_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for this JSON configuration entry within the system configuration group.

plainFields.name: json_value
plainFields.description: The actual JSON configuration data stored as a string with proper JSON schema validation.

plainFields.name: json_schema
plainFields.description: JSON schema definition used to validate the json_value field for type safety.

plainFields.name: version

Each record represents a business context associated with an error logged in {@link todo_app_error_logs}, capturing information about the operation being performed, affected entities, and workflow state at the time of the error. The table maintains referential integrity with the main error logs table and supports comprehensive error analysis by preserving the business context in which errors occurred.

models.name: todo_app_system_configuration_number_validations
models.description:
Stores validation constraints for numeric configuration values, including minimum and maximum value limits, validation rules, and constraint metadata. This table ensures that numeric configuration values adhere to specified constraints and provides comprehensive validation rules for system configuration management.

Each validation record corresponds to exactly one numeric configuration value in {@link todo_app_system_configuration_numbers}, establishing a 1:1 relationship for constraint enforcement. The validation constraints include minimum and maximum value limits, validation type categorization, and constraint metadata that configuration values must satisfy.

This table supports the systematic component's configuration management system by providing validation rules that maintain data integrity, prevent invalid configuration values from being applied to the system, and enable audit trail tracking through soft deletion capabilities.

Common validation types include: 'range' (minimum/maximum constraints), 'positive_only' (values > 0), 'non_negative' (values >= 0), 'integer_only' (whole numbers only), and custom constraint definitions.

plainFields.name: maximum_value

plainFields.name: validation_type

plainFields.name: constraint_description

Stores environment-specific debugging information including variables and configuration values that provide context for error debugging.

This table captures the runtime environment state at the time an error occurred, including environment variables, configuration settings, and system context that can help developers reproduce and debug issues. models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Main todo entity storing core information about user tasks.

This table represents the central Todo entity that users create, manage, and track. Todos are owned by individual users and contain basic identification information while delegating optional fields like descriptions and dates to specialized child tables for better normalization.

The {@link todo_app_todo_completions} child table tracks completion status, {@link todo_app_todo_description_fields} handles optional descriptions, and date fields are managed by {@link todo_app_todo_start_date_fields} and {@link todo_app_todo_due_date_fields} respectively. Edit history is maintained through the {@link todo_app_todo_histories} table in the History component, while soft deletion is handled through the Trash component tables.

Todos support comprehensive lifecycle management including creation, editing, completion tracking, and deletion with recovery capabilities. Each operation is audited through the integrated history tracking system.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: Owner of this todo. References the creator/user's {@link todo_app_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title or name of the todo task. Required field that provides the primary identifier for the task.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was initially created. Used for chronological ordering and audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last modified. Used for tracking recent activity and synchronization.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was soft-deleted. Null indicates active todo, non-null indicates moved to trash.

models.name: todo_app_todo_completions
models.description:
Tracks completion status changes for todos with timestamps for audit trail and edit history integration.

Each record represents a specific completion state change event, allowing the system to track when todos were marked as complete or incomplete. This supports comprehensive edit history functionality and provides an audit trail for completion status modifications.

Records reference the parent {@link todo_app_todos.id} and capture the exact timestamp of status changes to enable chronological analysis of todo lifecycle events.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent todo being tracked for completion status changes. {@link todo_app_todos.id}

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the todo was marked as completed (true) or incomplete (false) in this status change event.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this completion status change was recorded for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this completion record was soft deleted, supporting undo functionality for completion tracking deletions.

models.name: todo_app_todo_completion_statuses
models.description:
Tracks individual completion status change events for todos with timestamps and audit trail.

Each record represents a distinct status change event for a todo, providing comprehensive auditing and tracking of completion state transitions. This table enables detailed analysis of todo completion patterns and supports recovery operations by maintaining a complete history of completion status changes.

Records the timestamp of each status change event. {@link todo_app_todo_completions.id} tracks which completion record this status change belongs to.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_completion_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent completion record's {@link todo_app_todo_completions.id} for audit trail association.

plainFields.name: changed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this completion status change occurred.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status change record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status change record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status change record was soft deleted, if applicable.

models.name: todo_app_todo_description_fields
models.description:
Stores optional description text for todos, allowing the main todo table to avoid nullable description fields.

This table implements a common pattern for handling optional fields by separating them into a dedicated table with a 1:1 relationship to the parent entity. When a todo has a description, this table contains the text; when no description is provided, no record exists in this table.

The description field supports rich text content and is indexed for search capabilities. This design maintains data integrity while providing flexibility for optional content storage.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent todo. {@link todo_app_todos.id}

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: The optional description text for the todo. Supports rich content and can be left empty if no description is provided.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the description field was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the description field was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_todo_start_date_fields
models.description:
Stores optional start dates for todos with validation and formatting support.

This table provides a normalized approach to handling optional start dates by separating them from the main todo table. Each record represents a start date associated with a specific todo, allowing for proper validation and formatting while maintaining referential integrity.

The start date field supports date validation to ensure logical consistency with other todo dates, particularly with due dates. This separation allows for efficient querying of todos with specific date ranges while keeping the main todo table focused on core attributes.

Records in this table are managed through their parent {@link todo_app_todos} entity and inherit the lifecycle management of the associated todo.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent todo entity. {@link todo_app_todos.id}

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: The optional start date for the todo. Can be null if no start date is specified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this start date record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this start date record was last updated.

models.name: todo_app_todo_due_date_fields
models.description:
Stores optional due dates for todos with cross-validation capabilities against start dates. This table maintains the due date information separately from the main todo entity to handle optional fields properly.

Each due date entry is associated with exactly one todo and supports the business requirement of optional deadline tracking. The due date is used for sorting, filtering, and deadline management functionality. When both start date and due date are provided, the system validates that the due date is not before the start date.

This table works in conjunction with {@link todo_app_todo_start_date_fields} to provide comprehensive date management for todo scheduling and deadline tracking. All temporal tracking is maintained through the parent {@link todo_app_todos} entity.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent todo. {@link todo_app_todos.id}

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for the todo. Used for deadline tracking and scheduling. Supports cross-validation with start date when both are provided.

models.name: todo_app_todo_histories
models.description:
Main history table that records each edit operation performed on todos with timestamp and user context. This table serves as the primary audit trail for todo modifications, capturing when changes were made and by whom. Each entry represents a distinct edit event that may involve changes to title, description, start date, or due date fields. The history entries are immutable once created and provide comprehensive tracking for compliance and user transparency.

This table works in conjunction with child tables that track individual field changes, ensuring proper normalization and granular audit capabilities. Users can view complete edit histories for each todo, including who made changes and when specific fields were modified.

plainFields.name: updated_at

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the history entry was soft deleted. Used for audit trail preservation while supporting cleanup operations.

models.name: todo_app_todo_history_changes
models.description:
Field-level change tracking that records specific field modifications within each history entry.

This table captures individual field changes that occur during todo edits, providing granular audit trail capabilities. Each record represents a single field modification within a broader edit operation recorded in {@link todo_app_todo_histories}. The table supports tracking changes to title, description, start date, and due date fields with both previous and new values stored for complete change history.

The design ensures comprehensive audit capabilities while maintaining data integrity through proper foreign key relationships and indexing strategies.

models.name: todo_app_todo_history_snapshots
models.description:
Tracks the creation of history snapshots for audit trail purposes. This table records when snapshots are generated from todo history entries, serving as metadata for the snapshot creation process rather than storing the actual snapshot data.

Each entry represents a snapshot generation event, linking back to the specific history entry that triggered the snapshot creation. This table works in conjunction with {@link todo_app_todo_histories} to track snapshot operations and with the actual snapshot storage tables for complete audit trail functionality.

The primary purpose is to maintain an audit trail of when snapshots were created, allowing the system to track snapshot generation patterns and manage snapshot lifecycle operations.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_history_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the history entry that triggered this snapshot creation. {@link todo_app_todo_histories.id}

plainFields.name: snapshot_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot event was recorded, representing when the snapshot generation occurred.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot event record was created in the database.

models.name: todo_app_history_metadata
models.description:
System metadata table for history tracking configuration and cleanup management.

This table stores configuration settings, cleanup policies, retention periods, and operational metadata for the history tracking system. It supports the main history tables by providing system-level configuration and management capabilities.

The metadata includes settings for automatic cleanup operations, retention policies for historical data, and configuration parameters that control how the history system operates. This ensures consistent behavior across the history tracking functionality and provides audit trails for system operations.

{@link todo_app_todo_histories} and other history tables reference these configuration settings to determine retention periods and cleanup behavior.

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_items
models.description:
Stores denormalized point-in-time snapshots of todo states for comprehensive audit trail purposes.

This table captures the complete state of todos at specific edit moments, including all fields (title, description, start date, due date, completion status) in a denormalized format optimized for audit trail queries. Each snapshot item represents the state of a todo at a specific point in time, allowing for complete historical reconstruction and audit trail functionality.

The denormalized structure ensures that audit trail queries can retrieve complete todo states without requiring complex joins across multiple tables, making historical analysis and recovery operations more efficient. {@link todo_app_todo_history_snapshots} provides the parent snapshot context for each set of snapshot items.

This table is essential for supporting edit history viewing, undo operations, and compliance requirements where complete historical state information is necessary.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_id

plainFields.name: is_completed

models.name: todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_metadata
models.description:
Metadata table for tracking snapshot generation details and audit trail information.

This table stores metadata specifically related to todo history snapshot operations, including generation timing, system context, and audit trail information. It provides supplemental data for the snapshot generation process that doesn't belong in the main snapshot table.

Each metadata record is associated with a specific snapshot generation event and contains technical details about the generation process that support audit requirements and system monitoring. This metadata supports compliance requirements and provides visibility into snapshot operations without duplicating parent table attributes.

{@link todo_app_todo_history_snapshots} records reference this metadata for comprehensive audit trail support.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todo_history_snapshot_id

models.name: todo_app_trash_items
models.description:
Tracks soft-deleted todos and their trash metadata including deletion timestamp and restoration status. Each entry represents a todo that has been moved to trash but can potentially be restored. This table maintains the connection between the deleted todo and its original owner while tracking the deletion event.

When a user deletes a todo, a record is created here to track the deletion. If the todo is restored, the restoration status is updated. If permanently deleted, the record remains for audit purposes but the todo reference is cleared.

This table supports the trash management workflow by providing the necessary metadata for restoration operations and trash cleanup processes.

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: todo_app_trash_restorations
models.description:
Records restoration events when users restore deleted todos from trash back to active status.

Each restoration event captures when a user restores a previously deleted todo back to active status, creating an audit trail for accidental deletion recovery operations. The table maintains references to both the user who performed the restoration and the specific trash item that was restored.

This table supports the application's safety features by providing complete visibility into restoration operations, enabling users to track their recovery actions and providing data isolation guarantees that ensure users can only access restoration events for their own todos.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_trash_item_id

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: todo_app_permanent_deletions
models.description:
Tracks permanent deletion operations for audit purposes and compliance requirements.

This table serves as an audit trail for when users permanently delete todos from the trash system. Each record captures who deleted what todo and when, providing comprehensive audit capabilities for compliance and user accountability.

Records in this table are append-only and represent the final step in the todo lifecycle when items are removed from the trash. The table references {@link todo_app_users.id} for user accountability and {@link todo_app_todos.id} for tracking which todo was permanently deleted.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record update timestamp for audit trail.

models.name: todo_app_trash_cleanup_logs

Logs automated trash cleanup operations and system-initiated permanent deletions for audit and monitoring purposes.

This table records all system-generated cleanup activities that permanently remove expired items from the trash. Each entry tracks operation details including processed item counts, success/failure status, cleanup criteria, and performance metrics. These logs provide audit trails for compliance requirements and system monitoring.

models.name: todo_app_trash_settings
models.description:
Stores user preferences for trash retention periods and cleanup automation settings.

Each user can configure personal preferences for how their deleted todos are managed in the trash system. This includes automatic cleanup timeframes, notification preferences, and retention policies that determine when items are permanently deleted from the trash.

The settings support flexible trash management while ensuring user control over data retention and cleanup automation. All settings default to system-wide values but can be customized per user to accommodate different workflow preferences.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_user_id
foreignFields.description: Associated user's {@link todo_app_users.id} who owns these trash settings.

plainFields.name: retention_period_days
plainFields.description: Number of days to keep items in trash before automatic cleanup. Default system value is 30 days.

plainFields.name: auto_cleanup_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether automatic cleanup of expired trash items is enabled for this user.

plainFields.name: notify_before_cleanup
plainFields.description: Whether to send notifications before items are automatically cleaned up from trash.

plainFields.name: notify_days_before
plainFields.description: Number of days before cleanup to send notification. Only relevant if notify_before_cleanup is true.

plainFields.name: permanent_deletion_confirmation
plainFields.description: Whether to require confirmation before permanently deleting items from trash.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when these trash settings were created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when these trash settings were last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when these trash settings were soft deleted (if applicable).

models.name: todo_app_trash_item_metadata
models.description:
Tracks supplemental metadata for trash items to support automated cleanup processes and retention management.

This table stores additional information needed for the trash management system beyond basic deletion tracking. It enables features like automated cleanup eligibility determination, retention period enforcement, and cleanup status tracking. The metadata supports compliance requirements and user configurable retention preferences.

Each record represents the cleanup and retention configuration for a single trash item from {@link todo_app_trash_items}. The table maintains critical timing information for automated cleanup decisions and provides status tracking for retention policy enforcement.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_trash_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the trash item being tracked. {@link todo_app_trash_items.id}

plainFields.name: cleanup_eligible
plainFields.description: Indicates if this trash item is eligible for automated cleanup based on retention policies.

plainFields.name: retention_expires_at
plainFields.description: Calculated timestamp when retention period expires and automated cleanup can occur.

plainFields.name: cleanup_scheduled_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when automated cleanup is scheduled to process this trash item.

plainFields.name: manual_cleanup_requested
plainFields.description: Flag indicating if user explicitly requested cleanup bypassing retention period.

plainFields.name: cleanup_processed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when automated cleanup was successfully processed.
